blocks.text: Hannibal Books publishes Regardez-moi / Look at Me by Jérôme Schlomoff .

Jérôme Schlomoff (born 1961) is a French photographer and filmmaker. Since 2005, he has lived and worked in Amsterdam. Since 1984, portraiture has been central to his work, with a particular interest in artists and the contemporary art world. In 1996, he developed Sténopés d’Architecture , a series exploring the links between architecture and photography by turning buildings into pinhole cameras. Since 2014, he has had a studio in the Jordaan district of Amsterdam. Portraiture, architecture and cinema form the core of his artistic practice. The interplay between these three disciplines is the foundation of his work.

In his latest book, Regardez-moi / Look at Me , he brings together portraits of contemporary artists and other creative figures made since 1984. Against a white background, without props and in precise framing, his black-and-white portraits reveal a subtle play of shadow and light. Regardez-moi / Look at Me is a raw exchange, a confrontation: one gaze challenging another.

The book gathers his one hundred most emblematic portraits, including those of Georg Baselitz, Jean-Michel Basquiat, Gilbert & George, Keith Haring, Panamarenko, Bill Viola, John Cale, Charlotte Gainsbourg, Juliette Gréco, Michael Stipe and Peter Greenaway. Each portrait is accompanied by a poetic text by Didier Arnaudet, in an intuitive layout designed by Irma Boom Office.

Didier Arnaudet’s texts—he is a French poet and art critic—are brief and incisive. They may be an anecdote, a memory, a distorted or imagined statement. The use of the formal “vous” introduces a tension between distance and a strange closeness, which intrigues and sometimes unsettles. It is sometimes hard to tell who is speaking: the sitter, the viewer or the photographer? This ambiguity opens the way to multiple interpretations and creates a fictional effect that brings the encounter between portrait and text to life.
